author: South Raleigh News
title: Mike Schietzelt highlights NC legislative victories and collaboration
text:
Mike Schietzelt, North Carolina State Representative for 35th District | www.facebook.com
Mike Schietzelt, North Carolina State Representative for 35th District | www.facebook.com
Mike Schietzelt, a representative for the North Carolina House, recently shared insights and updates on legislative developments through his social media platform. His posts highlight significant achievements in state legislation and personal reflections on collaborative efforts.
On July 9, 2025, Schietzelt announced a legislative milestone with the signing of SB 311, known as the "Law and Order Act," into law by Governor Roy Cooper. He expressed that "North Carolinians are safer today than we were yesterday." The bill represents a bipartisan victory aimed at enhancing safety for North Carolina drivers and protecting critical supply chain infrastructure. Schietzelt acknowledged his role in contributing to this legislative effort.
In another post on the same day, Schietzelt praised colleagues involved in recent legislative successes. He noted that "every great piece of legislation this year has had either @gachesser or @CampbellforNC working on it." This statement reflects his appreciation for their contributions to various bills throughout the year.
Schietzelt also made a cultural reference in a subsequent tweet posted seconds later. He mentioned a personal theory he calls the "Caine-Hackman Theory," while humorously stating his refusal to apologize for what he described as a niche movie reference. In this context, he recommended that "everyone should watch PCU at least once in their lives."
Additional information reveals that Mike Schietzelt is an active participant in North Carolina's legislative process, often engaging with fellow lawmakers such as Gale Chesser and John Campbell to advance policy initiatives.
